description: The roles of an anaesthetic record, written with no hospital in mind. A hospital's map supplies each role view as one SELECT over its own tables, and an audit written against the role views then runs unchanged at any hospital. roles.md, beside this file, explains each role in words.
rules: One row of role_anaesthetic is one anaesthetic, and its key identifies that anaesthetic and no other.
Every time is in local time, as the hospital's clocks showed it, and no view converts a time to another zone.
A reading, an event, a drug given or a device belongs to an anaesthetic by its link to that anaesthetic, and never because its time falls within the anaesthetic.
A role view keeps the rows that an audit leaves out, such as test patients, anaesthetics with no stop and values that were not accepted, so that the counts can see them.
A role view never joins in a way that repeats a row of the thing it describes, so that the view's key identifies its row.
An empty value means that the record does not say, and a value that the record holds but cannot be read as the role's type is also empty.
A key compares equal with itself within one hospital only, and no key is carried from one hospital to another.
A value is in the unit that its role or its kind fixes, and a view converts a value held in another unit.

views.name: role_patient
views.description: One row for each patient, test and training patients included, so that an audit can leave them out by is_test.
views.holds: The patient table of the hospital's system, which holds one row for each person; the date of death is often held in a second patient table or loaded from a registry.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the patient, the same value that role_anaesthetic.patient_key holds.
columns.holds: The patient table's own key.

columns.name: birth_date
columns.meaning: The date of birth, to the day, so that an age in days counts calendar dates.
columns.holds: The patient table.

columns.name: death_date
columns.meaning: The date of death where the hospital knows of it, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The patient table, a second patient table, or a table loaded from a death registry.

columns.name: is_test
columns.meaning: 1 for a test or training patient who is not a real person, and 0 for every other patient.
columns.holds: A flag on the patient table or a second patient table, or a naming convention that the hospital uses for test patients.

views.name: role_anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each episode of anaesthesia or sedation given by an anaesthetist, including those whose start or stop is missing or out of order, so that the counts can see them.
views.holds: The anaesthetic record or anaesthesia episode, which is usually its own table, linked to a theatre case or to an encounter of its own.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the anaesthetic, the same value that role_reading.anaesthetic_key holds.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record's own key.
look_for: unique id of the anaesthesia episode

columns.name: patient_key
columns.meaning: The patient who had the anaesthetic, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the encounter or theatre case to which it is linked.

columns.name: start_time
columns.meaning: When the anaesthetic started, in local time.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the anaesthesia start event of the theatre case.

columns.name: stop_time
columns.meaning: When the anaesthetic stopped, in local time, and empty where no stop was recorded.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the anaesthesia stop event of the theatre case.

views.name: role_reading
views.description: One row for each value charted in an anaesthetic's own record, with its kind from the vocabulary below, including values that were not accepted and values that are not numbers.
views.one_row_per: value charted in an anaesthetic's record
views.holds: A table of measurements or observations, often the largest in the system, with one row for each value of each kind at each moment, reached from the anaesthetic through the record or sheet on which it was charted.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic whose record holds the reading, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The sheet or record on which the reading was charted, which carries the anaesthetic's key or the key of the anaesthetic's own encounter.

columns.name: kind
columns.meaning: What was measured, as one of the kinds of the vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the reading that points at the system's own list of the things that can be charted.

columns.name: reading_time
columns.meaning: When the value was taken, in local time, and not when it was filed.
columns.holds: The reading itself, which often holds a second time at which the value was entered or received.

columns.name: value
columns.meaning: The value as a number in the kind's own unit, and empty where the charted value is not a number.
columns.holds: The reading itself, usually as text that holds numbers and words alike.

columns.name: accepted
columns.meaning: 1 where the value counts as valid, and 0 where it was marked as an artefact, rejected or superseded.
columns.holds: A flag on the reading, or the absence of the value after an edit, which the hospital's practice decides.

views.name: role_patient_detail
views.description: One row for each patient whose record holds any of these details, for the covariates of an audit.
views.holds: A second patient table, the birth history of the child, or the delivery record of the mother when it is linked to the baby.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.meaning: The patient, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The table that holds the details.

columns.name: sex
columns.meaning: The sex recorded at birth, as one of the kinds of the sex vocabulary.
columns.holds: The patient table, usually as a code with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: gestation_weeks
columns.meaning: The gestational age at birth in weeks, with any days as a fraction of a week.
columns.holds: The birth history, the newborn's delivery record, or a measurement charted on the newborn.

columns.name: birth_weight_grams
columns.meaning: The weight at birth in grams.
columns.holds: The birth history, the newborn's delivery record, or a measurement charted on the newborn.

views.name: role_stay
views.description: One row for each hospital stay, from admission to discharge, day stays included, for the length of stay and for readmission.
views.holds: The hospital encounter or admission table, which holds the admission and the discharge of each stay.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the stay, the same value that role_anaesthetic_detail.stay_key holds.
columns.holds: The encounter's own key.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.meaning: The patient whose stay it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: admit_time
columns.meaning: When the patient was admitted, in local time.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: discharge_time
columns.meaning: When the patient was discharged, or died in hospital, in local time, and empty while the patient is still in hospital.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: unplanned
columns.meaning: 1 for an emergency or other unplanned admission, 0 for a planned one, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The admission type or admission category of the encounter, as a code with a lookup table of names.

views.name: role_anaesthetic_detail
views.description: One row for each anaesthetic whose record holds any of these details, for the covariates and outcomes of an audit.
views.holds: Partly the anaesthetic record and partly the theatre case or surgical log, with the pre-anaesthetic assessment for the grade and the weight.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record's own key.
look_for: unique id of the anaesthesia episode

columns.name: stay_key
columns.meaning: The hospital stay in which the anaesthetic took place, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty where the anaesthetic belongs to no stay.
columns.holds: The theatre case or the anaesthetic record, which points at the admission, sometimes through a link table.

columns.name: technique
columns.meaning: The kind of anaesthetic, as one of the kinds of the technique vocabulary.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record or the theatre case, usually as a code, and sometimes several for one anaesthetic.

columns.name: asa_grade
columns.meaning: The ASA physical status grade from 1 to 6, without any letter for an emergency.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment, the anaesthetic record or the theatre case, usually as a code with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: is_emergency
columns.meaning: 1 where the operation was done as an emergency, 0 where it was planned, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The theatre case or booking, or an E after the ASA grade.

columns.name: weight_kg
columns.meaning: The patient's weight at the anaesthetic in kilograms.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment or a measurement charted on the day, and sometimes the theatre case.

columns.name: planned_icu
columns.meaning: 1 where intensive care after the operation was planned before it began, 0 where it was not, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The booking of the theatre case, as the planned destination after the operation or a request for an intensive care bed.

columns.name: unplanned_return
columns.meaning: 1 where the operation was recorded as an unplanned return to theatre, 0 where it was not, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The theatre case, where the hospital records an unplanned return as a reason or a flag.

views.name: role_operation
views.description: One row for each procedure done under an anaesthetic, so that an anaesthetic for several procedures has several rows.
views.holds: The procedures of the theatre case or surgical log, with a lookup table of the procedures that the hospital offers.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic under which the procedure was done, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The theatre case, which the anaesthetic record points at, or a link table between the two.

columns.name: procedure_code
columns.meaning: The hospital's own code of the procedure, or a national code where the hospital uses one.
columns.holds: The procedures of the theatre case.

columns.name: procedure_name
columns.meaning: The name of the procedure as the hospital's list gives it.
columns.holds: The lookup table of procedures, or the theatre case itself.

columns.name: specialty
columns.meaning: The surgical specialty of the procedure, as one of the kinds of the specialty vocabulary, which gives the operation's kind.
columns.holds: The service or specialty of the theatre case or of the surgeon.

columns.name: is_cardiac
columns.meaning: 1 where the procedure was a cardiac operation or a cardiac catheter procedure, 0 where it was not, and empty where nothing says.
columns.holds: The specialty of the theatre case, the procedure's own code, or a diagnosis of the stay.

views.name: role_unit_stay
views.description: One row for each period that a patient spent in one unit during a hospital stay, for admission to intensive care after an anaesthetic.
views.holds: The movements of the encounter, with one row for each transfer in or out of a unit, and a lookup table that says what kind of unit each one is.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.meaning: The hospital stay during which the patient was in the unit, as role_stay.stay_key.
columns.holds: The movement row.

columns.name: unit_kind
columns.meaning: The kind of unit, as one of the kinds of the unit vocabulary.
columns.holds: The department or unit of the movement, whose kind the hospital's list of units gives.

columns.name: entered_time
columns.meaning: When the patient entered the unit, in local time.
columns.holds: The movement row.

columns.name: left_time
columns.meaning: When the patient left the unit, in local time, and empty while the patient is still there.
columns.holds: The next movement row of the same stay.

views.name: role_event
views.description: One row for each timed milestone of an anaesthetic, such as induction, intubation, incision and extubation, with its kind from the event vocabulary.
views.holds: The events of the anaesthetic record or the timing events of the theatre case, each with a code for the kind of event.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The event row, or the theatre case that it belongs to.

columns.name: kind
columns.meaning: The kind of event, as one of the kinds of the event vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the event row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: event_time
columns.meaning: When the event happened, in local time.
columns.holds: The event row.

views.name: role_drug
views.description: One row for each dose given during an anaesthetic, and for each start, change of rate and stop of an infusion.
views.holds: The administrations of the medication record, linked to their orders, or drug values charted on the anaesthetic record.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic during which the drug was given, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The order of the drug, which belongs to the anaesthetic's own encounter.

columns.name: drug
columns.meaning: The drug, as the hospital's own name or code for it.
columns.holds: The order, with a lookup table of the hospital's medications.

columns.name: action
columns.meaning: What was done, as one of the kinds of the drug action vocabulary.
columns.holds: The administration row, as a code for the action.

columns.name: amount
columns.meaning: The dose, or the rate of an infusion, as a number in the unit beside it.
columns.holds: The administration row.

columns.name: unit
columns.meaning: The unit of the amount, as the hospital records it.
columns.holds: The administration row, as a code for the unit.

columns.name: route
columns.meaning: The route by which the drug was given, as the hospital records it.
columns.holds: The administration row or the order.

columns.name: given_time
columns.meaning: When the dose was given or the infusion changed, in local time.
columns.holds: The administration row, which often holds a second time at which it was charted.
look_for: time that the action took place

views.name: role_device
views.description: One row for each airway device, line or catheter placed for an anaesthetic, with its kind from the device vocabulary.
views.holds: The lines, drains and airways of the patient's record, each with its placement and removal.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic for which the device was placed, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The device row, where it carries the anaesthetic's key; otherwise the device belongs to the patient and the link must be found.

columns.name: kind
columns.meaning: The kind of device, as one of the kinds of the device vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the device row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: placed_time
columns.meaning: When the device was placed, in local time.
columns.holds: The device row.

columns.name: removed_time
columns.meaning: When the device was removed, in local time, and empty while it stays in place.
columns.holds: The device row.

types.key: Any type that compares equal with itself within one hospital, such as a whole number or text.
types.datetime: A date and a time of day, in local time.
types.number: A number that may hold a fraction.
types.flag: The whole number 1 or 0, and never empty.
types.flag_or_empty: The whole number 1 or 0, or empty where the record does not say.
types.kind: Text that is one of the kinds of the vocabulary that the column names.
types.text: Text as the hospital records it.

kinds.meaning: A mean arterial pressure from an arterial line, in mmHg.
A mean arterial pressure from a non-invasive cuff, in mmHg.
A heart rate, in beats a minute.
An oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry, in per cent.
An end-tidal carbon dioxide, in mmHg.
A body temperature, in degrees Celsius.
Any other value charted in the anaesthetic's record, which the counts use to see whether the record is reached at all.

sex.meaning: Any other value, or one that says nothing was recorded.

technique.meaning: A general anaesthetic, with or without a regional block.
A regional or neuraxial block without a general anaesthetic.
Sedation given by an anaesthetist, including monitored anaesthesia care.
Local anaesthesia with an anaesthetist in attendance.
Any other kind, or one that the record does not give.

specialty.meaning: Cardiac surgery and cardiac catheter procedures.
Imaging and other procedures outside theatre.

unit.meaning: An intensive care unit, neonatal, paediatric or adult.
An operating theatre or a procedure room.

event.meaning: The airway placed or the trachea intubated.

device.meaning: A laryngeal mask or other supraglottic airway.
An epidural or other regional catheter.

drug_action.meaning: The rate of an infusion changed.
A dose that was charted but not given.

outcomes.name: death_within_days
outcomes.meaning: Whether the patient died within a given number of days of the anaesthetic's start, counted by calendar date.

outcomes.name: unplanned_intensive_care
outcomes.meaning: Whether the patient entered intensive care within 24 hours after the anaesthetic's stop, when intensive care had not been planned and the patient was not already there at the start.

outcomes.name: return_to_theatre_30_days
outcomes.meaning: Whether the same patient had another anaesthetic with an operation within 30 days after this one's stop, and whether the hospital recorded that return as unplanned.

outcomes.name: length_of_stay
outcomes.meaning: The time from admission to discharge of the stay in which the anaesthetic took place, and the time from the anaesthetic's stop to that discharge.

outcomes.name: readmission_30_days
outcomes.meaning: Whether the patient began another unplanned stay within 30 days after the discharge of the stay in which the anaesthetic took place.
